title: Expression of CGRP in the Trigeminal Ganglion and Its Effect on the Polarization of Macrophages in Rats with Temporomand

predicted_errors.error_location: Abstract ('within 24 h ... significant surge in CD86 positive macrophages') vs. Results (TG macrophage quantification)
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The Abstract states there was 'a significant surge in CD86 positive macrophages within the ganglion' within 24 h of CFA injection, but the Results report that the day-1 comparison with control was non-significant (p = 0.7376). Only days 7 and 14 reached significance (p < 0.0001). The abstract therefore asserts a significant effect the data do not show.

predicted_errors.error_location: Results, behavioral testing paragraph (HWT after CFA)
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: 'A significant reduction in HWT was observed immediately following the injection... The HWT was notably reduced on days 1, 3, 7, and 14 post-injection when compared to controls (p = 0.2747, p = 0.0102, p = 0.0017, and p = 0.3946, respectively).' Two of the four listed p-values (day 1 = 0.2747; day 14 = 0.3946) exceed 0.05, so the claim of a notable/significant reduction at those time points — and the claim that HWT 'was still lower than the saline-injected control rats' at day 14 — is contradicted by the authors' own statistics.

predicted_errors.error_location: Results, TG injection of CGRP / CGRP 8-37 (Fig. 4B–D)
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: 'CD86-positive macrophages were significantly increased and decreased, respectively (p < 0.001 and p = 0.1939, respectively), while CD206-positive macrophages exhibited an inverse pattern (p = 0.6133 and p = 0.0403, respectively).' p = 0.1939 and p = 0.6133 are not significant, yet both are described as significant changes (CGRP decreasing CD86; CGRP 8-37 altering CD206). The text's descriptive claims do not match the reported p-values.

predicted_errors.error_location: Abstract ('injecting the CGRP receptor antagonist (CGRP 8-37) to the ganglion counteracts this shift towards the M2 phenotype')
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The only supporting datum for CD206 (M2) after CGRP 8-37 injection is p = 0.6133 (non-significant), and the Results themselves state there was 'no notable change in CD206 levels' after CGRP 8-37 in TMJ tissue. The abstract therefore overstates an effect that was not demonstrated.

'CD86-positive M1 macrophages significantly increased one day after CFA treatment, peaking at day 7' is immediately followed by '(p = 0.6672, p = 0.1276, p < 0.0001, p = 0.0033, respectively)' for days 1, 3, 7, 14. The day-1 (and day-3) comparisons were non-significant, contradicting the stated significant increase at 1 day.

predicted_errors.error_location: Methods, immunohistochemistry section ('Demineralized TMJs from two groups (CFA-treated, n = 6 joints; Saline-treated, n = 6 joints)')
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The IHC methods describe only two groups, but the IHC results (Fig. 5) report five conditions (control plus CFA at 1, 3, 7 and 14 days) and Fig. 6 reports three additional ganglion-injection groups (saline, CGRP, CGRP 8-37). The described sampling design cannot generate the reported data.

The abstract states that TMJ and TG tissues were collected and that 'immunohistochemistry, immunofluorescence (IF) staining, and RT-qPCR were used to examine the expression of CGRP and macrophage-related factors.' However, RT-qPCR is described only for cultured THP-1-derived macrophages (human CD86/CD206 primers), and no tissue RT-qPCR data are reported anywhere in the Results.

predicted_errors.error_location: Introduction ('during the chronic pain phase of OA, an upsurge in trigeminal ganglion's CGRP is observed (Duffadar et al. 2009; Miller et al. 2017)')
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: Duffadar et al. (2009) is a colloid/particle-adhesion paper and is implausible as a source for CGRP in sensory ganglia; moreover, the OA pain literature cited (Miller et al.) concerns knee OA and dorsal root ganglia, not trigeminal ganglion CGRP. The citations do not support the stated claim.

Catalogue numbers beginning with 'ab' are Abcam identifiers; ab81887 is an Abcam anti-CGRP antibody, not a Cell Signaling Technology (CST) product. The reagent source is misattributed, which prevents reproducibility.

After the primary antibody incubation, sections are described as being incubated directly with 'horseradish enzyme-labeled streptavidin solution' and then DAB. Streptavidin-HRP requires a biotinylated secondary antibody, which is never mentioned; as written, the detection chemistry cannot produce specific staining.

predicted_errors.error_location: Methods, immunofluorescence (primary/secondary antibody combination) vs. Results (Figs. 3A, 4B–C)
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: All three primaries (CGRP, CD206, CD86) are rabbit antibodies and only one secondary — goat anti-rabbit Alexa Fluor 488 — is described. Single-channel anti-rabbit detection cannot distinguish CD86 from CD206 (or CGRP from macrophage markers) within the same section, yet the Results describe simultaneous M1/M2 assessment and CD206-positive macrophages located around CGRP-expressing neurons.

predicted_errors.error_location: Methods (IHC antibodies) vs. Results (Fig. 5D, Fig. 6D CGRP IHC in TMJ)
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The IHC methods list only CD86 (Huabio ER1906) and CD206 (CST 24595) primary antibodies, but the Results report quantified CGRP immunohistochemical staining in TMJ tissue at all time points and after ganglion injections. No antibody, dilution, or protocol is given for the CGRP IHC.
